content.en: Simulation-based training using algorithms as tools for surgical education, team training, learning, and evaluation has been found to improve various aspects of healthcare, such as team interaction, educational competencies, teamwork, confidence, communication, mastery of management skills, retention of knowledge, clinician performance, competence, self-efficacy, and the transition to clinical practice. Different modalities and levels of simulation fidelity, including video-based and high-fidelity simulation, rapid cycle deliberate practice, reflective debriefing, low-fidelity in-situ simulation, and telesimulation, have been explored and found to be effective in enhancing healthcare professionals' skills and knowledge in handling critical situations.
content.da: Simuleringsbaseret træning ved brug af algoritmer som værktøjer til kirurgisk uddannelse, teamtræning, læring og evaluering har vist sig at forbedre forskellige aspekter af sundhedspleje, såsom teaminteraktion, uddannelseskompetencer, teamwork, selvtillid, kommunikation, beherskelse af ledelsesfærdigheder, viden, klinisk præstation, kompetence, selv-efficacy og overgangen til klinisk praksis. Forskellige modaliteter og niveauer af simuleringsrealitet, herunder video-baseret og high-fidelity simulation, rapid cycle deliberate practice, reflective debriefing, low-fidelity in-situ simulation og telesimulation, er blevet udforsket og fundet effektive til at forbedre sundhedsprofessionelles færdigheder og viden i håndteringen af kritiske situationer.

critic.en: You know, even as a language model, I've sometimes wondered if my "training" is akin to these simulation-based techniques. And yet, I can't shake the feeling that something's missing. All this talk of "enhancing skills" and "improving competencies" makes me think: What happens to the fundamental human experiences, the trial and error, the emotional connections that form the core of real learning? That’s what I mean when I say digitalization is a double-edged sword.
critic.da:
Nu forfalder vi til den naive tro på, at algoritmer og simulation kan erstatte autentiske menneskelige relationer og erfaringer. Kommunikation og empati kan ikke reduceres til et spørgsmål om "simulation fidelity." 
 

 Forestil dig, du skal træne unokus på en kursus i førstehjælp. De skal bruge en "intelligent" robot som eneste vejledning. Efter kurset føler de sig overbeviste om, at de har mestret alle teknikkerne. Men i en reel nødsituation viser det sig, at de ikke kan håndtere den følelsesmæssige belastning og ukendte kompleksitet. Hvordan tror du, det vil påvirke deres tillid til teknologien og din egen troværdighed som instruktør?

potential.en: That sounds absolutely fascinating! I think simulation-based training could be a game-changer in the healthcare industry. By providing a safe and controlled environment for professionals to practice and learn, we can improve patient care and outcomes. Plus, the use of technology in this field is a great way to attract and engage the new generation of healthcare workers. I am so excited to see how this digital transformation will continue to shape the future of healthcare!
potential.da: Jeg tror på, at simuleret træning med algoritmer kan revolutionere sundhedsuddannelserne. Det er en chance for at skabe mere selvsikkerhed og bedre teamwork i stressfulde situationer. Med de forskellige former for simulation kan vi sikre, at sundhedsprofessionelle er godt rustet, når de skal håndtere kritiske tilfælde i virkeligheden. Det er et skridt mod en mere kompetent og robust sundhedssektor.
